extraction.name: NWPU-RESISC45
extraction.description: NWPU-RESISC45 is a large-scale publicly available benchmark dataset for Remote Sensing Image Scene Classification (RESISC), created by Northwestern Polytechnical University (NWPU). It contains 31,500 images covering 45 scene classes with 700 images in each class, with image sizes of 256×256 pixels in RGB color space. The spatial resolution varies from about 30 m to 0.2 m per pixel. The dataset covers more than 100 countries and regions all over the world and features rich variations in translation, spatial resolution, viewpoint, object pose, illumination, background, and occlusion.
extraction.creator: Gong Cheng, Junwei Han, Xiaoqiang Lu; Northwestern Polytechnical University (NWPU)
extraction.citeAs: G. Cheng, J. Han, and X. Lu, 'Remote Sensing Image Scene Classification: Benchmark and State of the Art,' Proceedings of the IEEE.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were extracted from Google Earth (Google Inc.) by experts in the field of remote sensing image interpretation. The dataset covers more than 100 countries and regions all over the world, including developing, transition, and highly developed economies. Images were carefully selected under all kinds of weathers, seasons, illumination conditions, imaging conditions, and scales.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Satellite imagery, aerial photography, and geographic information system (GIS) data superimposed on a 3D globe via Google Earth (Google Inc.), covering more than 100 countries and regions worldwide.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Scene classes were selected by first investigating all scene classes of existing datasets to form 30 widely-used scene categories, then searching keywords on Web of Science and Google Scholar to select 15 additional meaningful scene classes, resulting in 45 total scene classes. Images were carefully selected under all kinds of weathers, seasons, illumination conditions, imaging conditions, and scales to ensure rich variations and high within-class diversity and between-class similarity.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were extracted from Google Earth as 256×256 pixel patches in the RGB color space. Fine-grained scene classes with high semantic overlapping were added (e.g., circular farmland and rectangular farmland, commercial area and industrial area, basketball court and tennis court).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Scene class labels were assigned by experts in the field of remote sensing image interpretation. The 45 scene classes include land use and land cover classes, man-made object classes, and landscape nature object classes.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Experts in the field of remote sensing image interpretation
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables the development and evaluation of new data-driven algorithms for remote sensing image scene classification, supporting applications such as natural hazards detection, land use and land cover determination, geospatial object detection, geographic image retrieval, vegetation mapping, environment monitoring, and urban planning.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Almost all existing scene classification methods rely on only traditional remote sensing (overhead imagery). The dataset does not incorporate social media geo-tagged ground photo collections or location-based geographic resources, which could complement traditional remote sensing for scene classification.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, and Validation of remote sensing image scene classification algorithms, including handcrafted feature-based methods, unsupervised feature learning methods, and deep learning-based methods. The dataset is intended as a benchmark for evaluating and comparing various data-driven algorithms for remote sensing image scene classification.
